```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
options(digits = 6, width = 95)
```

This vignette walks one real chamber closure through every step between the
raw 1 Hz record and the number that would be reported in a table, printing every
intermediate value. Nothing here is interactive, so the document can be rebuilt
with `rmarkdown::render()`.

## The closure

`stemflux` ships one closure, `2021-05-18_5086_I_7.0`: a 600 s tree-stem
measurement at Yale-Myers Forest (Connecticut) with a semi-rigid sleeve chamber
and an ABB/LGR micro-portable UGGA logging at 1 Hz. The chamber geometry comes
from the campaign auxfile and is stored by `example_closure()`:

| auxfile column | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Area`  | 4254.121 cm2 | stem surface enclosed |
| `Vtot`  | 7.082698 L | chamber + tubing + analyzer cell |
| `Tcham` | 26.02 C | chamber air temperature |
| `Pcham` | 101.325 kPa | pressure |

The rows carry the campaign's water column, so goFlux applies its water-vapour
correction to the flux term exactly as in the campaign processing.

```{r load}
library(stemflux)
d <- example_closure()
str(d[, c("UniqueID", "POSIX.time", "t_s", "CO2dry_ppm", "CH4dry_ppb", "flag", "Etime")])
```

The data frame is the campaign's `obs.win()` segment (the recorded
`start.time` plus a shoulder on each side) with the operator's clicked window
marked `flag = 1`, exactly as `goFlux::click.peak2()` left it.

```{r raw-plot, fig.height = 5}
w0 <- as.numeric(difftime(d$start.time_corr[1], d$start.time[1], units = "secs"))
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3, 4.5, 1.5, 1))
plot(d$t_s, d$CO2dry_ppm, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = ifelse(d$flag == 1, "grey20", "grey70"),
     xlab = "", ylab = "CO2 (ppm)", main = "obs.win segment; dark = clicked window, grey = context / dead band")
abline(v = c(0, w0, w0 + d$obs.length_corr[1]), col = c("blue", "red", "red"), lty = c(1, 2, 2))
plot(d$t_s, d$CH4dry_ppb, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = ifelse(d$flag == 1, "grey20", "grey70"),
     xlab = "seconds since recorded start.time", ylab = "CH4 (ppb)")
abline(v = c(0, w0, w0 + d$obs.length_corr[1]), col = c("blue", "red", "red"), lty = c(1, 2, 2))
par(op)
```

## Step 1: dead band (the clicked window)

The operator started the fitting window `r w0` s after the recorded closure
time (chamber mixing, operator disturbance) and ended it after
`r d$obs.length_corr[1]` s; that is the dead band as actually applied in the
campaign. The rows with `flag == 1` are what every fit below uses.

```{r deadband}
n_total <- nrow(d); n_used <- sum(d$flag == 1)
t_span  <- max(d$Etime[d$flag == 1]) - min(d$Etime[d$flag == 1])
c(n_total = n_total, n_used = n_used, window_start_s = w0, t_span_s = t_span)
```

## Step 2: fitted dC/dt

### 2a. Transparent linear fit

```{r lm}
w <- d[d$flag == 1, ]
fit_ch4 <- lm(CH4dry_ppb ~ Etime, data = w)
fit_co2 <- lm(CO2dry_ppm ~ Etime, data = w)
slope_ch4 <- unname(coef(fit_ch4)[2]); slope_co2 <- unname(coef(fit_co2)[2])
c(CH4_slope_ppb_per_s = slope_ch4, CH4_r2 = summary(fit_ch4)$r.squared,
  CH4_slope_SE = summary(fit_ch4)$coefficients[2, 2])
c(CO2_slope_ppm_per_s = slope_co2, CO2_r2 = summary(fit_co2)$r.squared)
```

### 2b. goFlux linear and Hutchinson-Mosier fits

`goFlux::goFlux()` fits both the linear model (LM) and the non-linear
Hutchinson-Mosier model (HM), and `goFlux::best.flux()` picks one using its
default criteria. goFlux prints a progress bar; it is captured here.

```{r goflux}
invisible(capture.output({
  res_ch4 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::goFlux(d, "CH4dry_ppb"))
  res_co2 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::goFlux(d, "CO2dry_ppm"))
}))
best_ch4 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::best.flux(res_ch4))
best_co2 <- suppressWarnings(goFlux::best.flux(res_co2))
as.data.frame(best_ch4[, c("LM.slope", "LM.r2", "LM.SE", "HM.slope", "HM.r2", "HM.k",
                           "model", "quality.check")])
```

`LM.slope` is the same number as the hand-rolled `lm()` above (`r signif(slope_ch4, 5)` ppb/s).

## Step 3: unit conversion

The gas columns are mole fractions: ppm = umol mol-1, ppb = nmol mol-1. A slope
in ppb s-1 is therefore already in nmol mol-1 s-1; converting to mol mol-1 s-1
is a factor of 1e-9.

```{r units}
slope_ch4_molfrac <- slope_ch4 * 1e-9   # mol mol-1 s-1
slope_co2_molfrac <- slope_co2 * 1e-6
c(CH4 = slope_ch4_molfrac, CO2 = slope_co2_molfrac)
```

## Step 4: V/A and P/RT

```{r geometry}
Area_m2 <- 4254.121 / 1e4
Vtot_m3 <- 7.082698 / 1e3
T_K     <- 26.02 + 273.15
P_Pa    <- 101.325 * 1e3
R       <- 8.314
VA      <- Vtot_m3 / Area_m2          # m
PRT     <- P_Pa / (R * T_K)           # mol m-3 (molar density of air)
c(V_over_A_m = VA, P_over_RT_mol_m3 = PRT, product_mol_m2 = VA * PRT)
```

`flux_term()` is the same product written with goFlux's unit conventions
(litres, kPa, cm2, Celsius). goFlux also multiplies by `(1 - H2O_mol)`, the
mean water-vapour mole fraction of the window, to express the flux per mole
of *dry* air; that is why its `flux.term` is slightly smaller than the dry
product:

```{r fluxterm}
h2o <- mean(w$H2O_ppm) / 1e6                          # mol mol-1
ft0 <- flux_term(V_L = 7.082698, P_kPa = 101.325, A_cm2 = 4254.121, T_C = 26.02)
ft  <- flux_term(V_L = 7.082698, P_kPa = 101.325, A_cm2 = 4254.121, T_C = 26.02, H2O_mol = h2o)
c(flux_term_dry = ft0, H2O_mol = h2o, flux_term_with_H2O = ft, goFlux_flux.term = best_ch4$flux.term)
```

## Step 5: flux

```{r flux}
flux_ch4_mol   <- slope_ch4_molfrac * VA * PRT * (1 - h2o)        # mol m-2 s-1, dry-air basis
flux_ch4_nmol  <- flux_ch4_mol * 1e9                              # nmol m-2 s-1
flux_co2_umol  <- slope_co2_molfrac * VA * PRT * (1 - h2o) * 1e6  # umol m-2 s-1
c(CH4_flux_nmol_m2_s = flux_ch4_nmol, CO2_flux_umol_m2_s = flux_co2_umol)
# the shortcut used by goFlux: slope in ppb/s times flux.term gives nmol m-2 s-1 directly
c(shortcut = slope_ch4 * ft, goFlux_LM = best_ch4$LM.flux, goFlux_HM = best_ch4$HM.flux,
  goFlux_best = best_ch4$best.flux)
```

## Step 6: per-measurement precision

Instrument noise is estimated from the measurement itself, not the datasheet.
First differences remove the (linear) flux signal; white noise survives with
variance 2 sigma^2, so sigma = SD(diff(x)) / sqrt(2).

```{r precision}
sigma_ch4 <- precision_allan(w$CH4dry_ppb)
sigma_co2 <- precision_allan(w$CO2dry_ppm)
c(sigma_CH4_ppb = sigma_ch4, sigma_CO2_ppm = sigma_co2,
  datasheet_CH4_ppb = 0.9, datasheet_CO2_ppm = 0.35,
  robust_MAD_CH4_ppb = precision_mad(w$CH4dry_ppb))
```

This analyzer was about 2.5 times noisier in CH4 than its datasheet claims,
which is why datasheet precision should not be used for detection limits.

## Step 7: minimum detectable flux by each method, by hand

```{r mdf}
t_used <- max(w$Etime) + 1     # goFlux's t; = nb.obs at 1 Hz
mdf <- mdf_multi(flux.term = ft, t = t_used,
                 prec = 0.9,               # manufacturer, for the goFlux method
                 sigma = sigma_ch4,        # this closure (Christiansen, 2-sigma)
                 sigma.global = sigma_ch4) # a campaign median would go here (Wassmann)
t(round(mdf, 6))
# by hand, Table 2.5 criterion: (2 sigma / t) (V/A) (P/RT)
c(MDF_2sigma_by_hand = (2 * sigma_ch4 * 1e-9 / t_used) * VA * PRT * (1 - h2o) * 1e9)
```

All MDFs are in nmol m-2 s-1. The regression standard error of the slope
(`LM.SE` = `r signif(best_ch4$LM.SE, 3)` nmol m-2 s-1) is far smaller than any of
them, which is the expected behaviour of these single-sample criteria.

## Step 8: precision, MDF and detection flag with `flag_detection()`

`flag_detection()` does steps 6-7 for every row of a `best.flux()` table with
*one* precision estimator and *one* MDF method and appends exactly six
columns: `sigma_emp`, `MDF_emp`, `below_MDF_emp`, `MDF_emp_method`,
`detected_emp`, `det_class_emp`. The default is the method of the companion
data-processing manuscript: sigma = MAD(diff x)/sqrt(2) over the *entire*
1 Hz record of the field period (here: this closure's whole trace, dead band
included), and MDF = z sigma / t flux.term. The stated confidence is 95%
two-sided, z = qnorm(0.975) = 1.96, i.e. the 2-sigma criterion (the companion
manuscript itself used z = qnorm(0.95) = 1.645, its "90% confidence"). goFlux's own columns
(`MDF`, `prec`, `best.flux`, ...) are left exactly as `best.flux()` produced
them. Nothing is deleted; rows are flagged.

```{r flag}
rep_ch4 <- flag_detection(best_ch4, traces = d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                          precision = "mad", mdf = "wassmann", conf = 0.95)   # the defaults, spelled out
setdiff(names(rep_ch4), names(best_ch4))
t(as.data.frame(rep_ch4[, c("MDF", "sigma_emp", "MDF_emp", "MDF_emp_method", "below_MDF_emp",
                            "detected_emp", "det_class_emp")]))
```

The multi-method comparison of step 7 is available as *extra* columns
(`sigma_<precision>`, `MDF_<method>_<precision>[_<conf>]`) for cross-study
reporting; they never replace the `*_emp` columns:

```{r extra}
cmp <- flag_detection(best_ch4, traces = d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                      extra = list(precision = c("allan", "mad", "datasheet"),
                                   mdf = c("goflux", "wassmann", "christiansen", "two_sigma"),
                                   conf = c(0.90, 0.95, 0.99)))
mdf_cols <- setdiff(grep("^MDF_[a-z]+_[a-z]", names(cmp), value = TRUE), "MDF_emp_method")
t(round(as.data.frame(cmp[, mdf_cols]), 6))
```

`MDF_goflux_datasheet` reproduces goFlux's own `MDF` column (same formula,
`t = nb.obs` instead of `max(Etime) + 1`); `MDF_wassmann_mad_95` is the
default `MDF_emp`.

## Choosing precision and MDF

The default is fixed by the companion data-processing manuscript; the others
are there so a report can state which one it used and readers can convert.
Each method by its actual formula and origin:

**Precision estimators**

| estimator | formula | computed over | origin / use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mad` (default) | MAD(diff x) x 1.4826 / sqrt(2) | the entire 1 Hz record of a field period (`group`) | companion manuscript (`mdf_FINAL_precision_and_detection.R`): instrument-dominated at 1 s, a constant flux cancels, robust to moves and breaths |
| `allan` | SD(diff x)/sqrt(2) | flagged rows of each closure | Allan deviation at tau = 1 s; per-closure noise |
| `rolling` | median residual SD of the quietest 5 percent of 30-sample windows | flagged rows of each closure | comparison only; biased low on white noise |
| `datasheet` | the `prec` value given to `goFlux::import.*()` | -- | manufacturer 1-s specification (2.5x too optimistic here) |
| `custom` | user-supplied `sigma` | bench test | Box 2 of the guidelines paper (sealed / standard-gas run) |

**MDF methods** (all `= dC_min / t x flux.term`)

| method | dC_min | origin |
|---|---|---|
| `wassmann` (default) | z x sigma_global, z = qnorm(1 - (1 - conf)/2); `conf = 0.95` gives z = qnorm(0.975) = 1.96, so the default is the 2-sigma criterion | Wassmann et al. (2018), PLoS ONE 13, e0191352; with the record-wide MAD sigma this is the companion manuscript's MDF form (that manuscript used `conf = 0.90`, z = 1.645) |
| `goflux` | p, the `prec` given at import | goFlux's built-in `MDF()`; goFlux's documentation cites Christiansen et al. (2015) for it |
| `christiansen` | sigma_i x 3 x t_crit(df = nb.obs - 2), two-sided | as implemented in the author's processing scripts under that name; the factor 3 is those scripts' safety factor and is not attributed here to Christiansen et al. (2015) or Nickerson (2016), whose text was not checked |
| `two_sigma` | 2 sigma_i | the illustration of Table 2.5 of the guidelines paper |

**Which to use for what.** Campaign means, budgets and upscaling: keep every
flux and report the fraction below `MDF_emp`; removing values biases means.
"Is this one flux non-zero?": the per-closure variants (`christiansen`,
`two_sigma` with `allan`) use the closure's own noise. Cross-study
comparison: `extra = "all"` and report the table.

**Where each is set in the pipeline.** The `prec` argument given to
`goFlux::import.*()` (or the `*_prec` columns) only feeds goFlux's own `MDF`
column and the `MDF` criterion inside `best.flux()`. stemflux's estimators are
applied *after* `best.flux()` by `flag_detection()`, which reads the flagged
traces and appends `sigma_emp`, `MDF_emp`, `below_MDF_emp`, `MDF_emp_method`
(and the `extra` comparison columns if asked). goFlux's columns are never
modified. Nothing is deleted at any step: `det_class_emp` says
`"below detection"`, and the row stays.

## Step 9: quality screens

Physical checks, each an independent flag (`TRUE` = fired), never a deletion.
Is the CO2 tracer positive (the chamber was sealed and respiration
accumulated)? Did the chamber start near ambient? Is the trace convex? Is the
window long enough? With one measurement the C0 screen compares the closure to
itself, so it passes trivially; in a campaign the median is taken over all
closures.

```{r qc}
rep_ch4 <- qc_screens(rep_ch4, traces = d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb", co2 = best_co2,
                      screens = list(c0 = list(k = 1.5), co2_tracer = list(min_slope = 0),
                                     convex = TRUE, min_window = list(secs = 120)),
                      verbose = FALSE)
t(as.data.frame(rep_ch4[, c("qc_c0", "qc_c0_ratio", "qc_co2_tracer", "qc_co2_slope", "qc_convex",
                            "qc_min_window", "qc_any", "qc_note")]))
```

## The reported row

```{r report}
report <- data.frame(
  UniqueID   = rep_ch4$UniqueID,
  n_obs      = rep_ch4$nb.obs,
  model      = rep_ch4$model,
  CH4_flux_nmol_m2_s = signif(rep_ch4$best.flux, 4),
  CH4_LM_SE  = signif(rep_ch4$LM.SE, 3),
  MDF_goFlux = signif(rep_ch4$MDF, 4),
  sigma_emp_ppb = signif(rep_ch4$sigma_emp, 3),
  MDF_emp    = signif(rep_ch4$MDF_emp, 3),
  MDF_emp_method = rep_ch4$MDF_emp_method,
  detected_emp = rep_ch4$detected_emp,
  class      = rep_ch4$det_class_emp,
  CO2_flux_umol_m2_s = signif(best_co2$best.flux, 4),
  qc_any     = rep_ch4$qc_any)
t(report)
```

The same row comes out of the one-call wrapper:

```{r wrapper}
invisible(capture.output(       # goFlux's progress bar is captured
  res <- suppressWarnings(process_fluxes(d, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                       qc = list(c0 = TRUE, co2_tracer = TRUE, convex = TRUE, min_window = list(secs = 120)),
                       co2 = best_co2))))
res
c(best.flux = res$fluxes$best.flux, MDF_goFlux = res$fluxes$MDF, MDF_emp = res$fluxes$MDF_emp,
  method = res$fluxes$MDF_emp_method)
all(names(best_ch4) %in% names(res$fluxes))   # goFlux columns all present, unchanged
```

## Summary of the numbers

```{r summary, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  quantity = c("observations used", "fit span (s)", "CH4 slope (ppb/s)", "CH4 LM r2",
               "V/A (m)", "P/RT (mol m-3)", "flux.term (mol m-2)",
               "CH4 flux LM (nmol m-2 s-1)", "CH4 flux HM (nmol m-2 s-1)", "CH4 flux reported",
               "sigma CH4 (ppb, Allan, flagged rows)", "sigma CH4 (ppb, MAD, whole record) = sigma_emp",
               "MDF goFlux (datasheet, goFlux's own column)",
               "MDF Wassmann 95% (mad) = MDF_emp", "MDF Christiansen-style 95% (allan)", "MDF 2-sigma (allan)",
               "reported MDF_emp / method", "detected", "CO2 flux (umol m-2 s-1)"),
  value = c(n_used, t_span, signif(slope_ch4, 5), signif(summary(fit_ch4)$r.squared, 4),
            signif(VA, 5), signif(PRT, 5), signif(ft, 5),
            signif(best_ch4$LM.flux, 5), signif(best_ch4$HM.flux, 5), signif(best_ch4$best.flux, 5),
            signif(sigma_ch4, 4), signif(rep_ch4$sigma_emp, 4), signif(best_ch4$MDF, 4),
            signif(cmp$MDF_wassmann_mad_95, 4), signif(cmp$MDF_christiansen_allan_95, 4),
            signif(cmp$MDF_two_sigma_allan, 4),
            paste(signif(rep_ch4$MDF_emp, 4), rep_ch4$MDF_emp_method), rep_ch4$det_class_emp,
            signif(best_co2$best.flux, 5))))
```
